sources.translator: Aylmer Maude (d. 1938); first published in English 1921 (World's Classics); Standard Ebooks transcription from the Wikisource/HathiTrust text

Standard Ebooks single-page HTML; confirm chapter numerals I-XVI in the fetched text and that it is the 1921 Maude text, not the joint Aylmer and Louise Maude revision (Louise d. 1939, also qualifies).

sources.what: Instruction of Amenemope, chapters 1-7 (the passages Proverbs 22:17-24:22 resembles)
sources.note: No online plain text of Griffith 1926 (or Budge 1924) found. Teach in our own words, with at most one short quotation, and set the parallel lines of Proverbs 22:17-21 (WEB) instead. Session 3's compare becomes Proverbs 22:17-21 against a description of Amenemope's prologue.

sources.what: Bernard of Clairvaux, Sermons on the Song of Songs, Sermon 1
sources.translator: Samuel J. Eales (1895, Cantica Canticorum: Eighty-six Sermons); only page images found (HathiTrust 012435481)
sources.note: PLEASE CHECK: the archive.org item stbernardssermon01bern appears to be 'St Bernard's Sermons on the Canticle of Canticles' (Dublin, Browne & Nolan, 1920, 'a Priest of Mount Melleray', probably Ailbe J. Luddy): published before 1929, but the translator's death year is unconfirmed, and the item may instead be his Sermons for the Seasons. Use it only if the translator died before 1955; otherwise plan Bernard in our own words. Eales 1895 is the qualifying text but has no fetchable text found.

art.why: No NGA painting of David as harpist or psalmist; castagno-david (David with the head of Goliath) is used elsewhere and is not the psalmist.
No NGA mourner or Jeremiah free: the Mourning Madonna and Mourning Saint John (Master of the Franciscan Crucifixes) are claimed by epicureans-and-stoics and suffering.
No Solomon in the NGA open data; the scholars and philosophers (Rembrandt workshop, Dou's Hermit) are used or claimed.

art.title: The Adoration of the Skulls
art.why: A memento mori: hooded men bowing before an altar of skulls, the nearest holding up a cross. Ecclesiastes faces death head on; the vanitas still lifes were claimed, and this is the clearest free image of the same thought.

art.title: Solitude
art.why: A man lying alone, his head covered with a cloth, beside a broken stone lion by still water: the solitude of Psalm 88 and of Tolstoy at the edge. (Daylight, not night: say so if used.)

art.title: Madonna and Child in a Garden
art.why: The enclosed-garden picture of the Virgin grew from the Song's 'garden locked up' (Song 4:12) read allegorically: the tradition's reading made visible. Check the description for the garden before writing look points.

art.title: Saint John the Evangelist
art.why: The writer of John 1, standing under an arch on gold: the Word session. No painting of Christ as Logos was free.

music.why: Psalm 23 sung to Crimond: the most sung psalm in Britain, as the Psalms were made to be sung.
Psalm 51 sung in the darkened Sistine Chapel: lament made into music.
No setting of Proverbs or Psalm 1 in music.json; this old Irish prayer asks for wisdom ('Be thou my wisdom') as Proverbs does.
Brahms sets 'All flesh is as grass' and 'Lord, teach me that there must be an end of me': Ecclesiastes' themes in a German Protestant requiem.
A symphony of lament that does not hurry to comfort: the right sound for the objection.
'Where charity and love are, God is there': the love the Song celebrates, read as the tradition read it.
The Orthodox all-night vigil, built of psalms: the Psalter as the Church still prays it.

flags: Sessions 1-3 have no painting (none of the subject is free in the NGA open data).
Amenemope: no qualifying online text found (Griffith 1926, Budge 1924); taught in our own words.
Bernard Sermon 1: Eales 1895 exists only as page images; the archive.org 1920 Mount Melleray text needs its translator's dates confirmed before use.
Tolstoy Confession: Standard Ebooks (Maude) single page is the source; not on Gutenberg under Maude.
Psalm 13 is read in session 1's compare and again in session 2's compare (spec says 'read again'); Psalm 88 is read in session 2 and recalled in session 5: Stage B should point back, not reprint.
Lowth, Augustine on the Psalms, Bonhoeffer, Lewis, Brueggemann, Alter, Schopenhauer and Mishnah Yadayim 3:5 are in our own words (no set text planned).
